title: CatalogFile
description: One catalog file (`catalog/<group>.toml`): a group and its commands.

group.description: Group name: `core` or the name of an optional group.

Group of the command; empty in catalog files, where the group is
given once per file.

effects.description: Actions whose effect differs from the command default.

waits.description: The command always blocks the call by waiting (`sleep`).

os.description: Operating systems the command is limited to; empty means all.

external.description:
Use of an external program or system component beyond the
implementation marker.

fallback.description:
Implementation used when the primary one is unavailable (syntax
analysis when no language server is installed).

required_groups.description:
Exclusive groups of which exactly one parameter must be given in the
primary form.

form.description: Input-dependent forms; empty when the command has a single form.

Category.description: Category of a command in the catalog.

oneOf.description: Starts a pipeline by producing records.
Transforms a record stream.
Checks a record stream or an effect.
Changes files, content or other local state.
Runs a program.
Inspects or administers the operating system.
Inspects or manages the operation journal.
Provides help and descriptions.
The command only reads; there is nothing to reverse.
The command is always reversible from the journal.

The command is reversible when the previous content was preserved;
otherwise the report marks it as irreversible.
The command is irreversible by nature.

EffectKind.description: Kind of effect a stage has on the world, recorded in the bound tree.

oneOf.description: Reads state only; no effect outside the process.
Changes local files or content; recorded in the journal and reversible.

Has an effect outside the local file system (network, services, remote
systems); not reversible by the journal.

Runs a user program whose effects are detected and classified after it
finishes.

Implementation.description: How a command is implemented with respect to external programs.

oneOf.description: Fully built into the executable.
Runs a program supplied by the user.
Acts as a client of an external language server.
Wraps the package manager of the operating system.

Uses a component of the operating system that has no public
programming interface; explicitly marked in the catalog.

IoSpec.description: Kind of stage input or output: none, any, same (output only), a scalar type keyword, or a record kind.

ActionEffect.description: Effect of one action of a command that differs from the command default.

action.description:
Identifier of the action: a value of the `action` parameter, a value of
another enumeration parameter (`method: post`), the name of a parameter
whose use changes the effect (`save`), or the input record kind for
commands whose effect depends on the kind of input (`job`); `note`
states the condition when it is not obvious.

note.description: Conditions of reversibility or other remarks.

Os.description: Operating system family a command is limited to.

oneOf.description: Linux.
Apple macOS.
Windows.

ExternalUse.description: Use of a program or a system component outside the executable.

programs.description: Names of the programs used (for example `launchctl`, `apt`).

when.description:
Parameter whose use triggers the external use; absent when the use is
unconditional.

note.description: Remark shown in the description and in the report.

ParamSpec.description: Specification of one parameter of a command.

position.description:
Position among the positional parameters of the primary form,
counted from 1; absent for named-only parameters.

required.description: The parameter is required in the primary form.

repeated.description: The positional parameter collects several arguments into a list.

per_record.description: The value may be an expression evaluated on each input record.

default.description: Default value as a literal of the language; absent means no value.

default_from.description:
Parameter whose value is the default: another parameter of the
command or the call parameter `base`. The value is converted to the
type of this parameter, so a path becomes a one-element list. A
required parameter with this key is missing only when its source has
no value either.

default_note.description:
Description of a default that is computed rather than literal (for
example "the latest operation").

values.description: Enumeration values of the type, repeated for readability.

exclusive_group.description: Name of a group of mutually exclusive parameters.

waits.description:
A value of this parameter above the waiting threshold makes the call
block; such stages are marked `waits` in the bound tree.

secret.description:
The value is confidential (credentials in an address or a header); it
is masked in the journal, the report and the printed bound tree.

ParamType.description: Type expression: scalars (text, int, number, bool, path, glob, regex, size, duration, percent, instant, key, bytes, range, expression, pipeline, field, named_expression, any), enum(a|b), list<T>, map<T>, stream<R> and alternatives A | B.

DefaultValue.description:
Default value of a parameter, written as a literal of the language in
variant A (`1`, `true`, `"**"`, `asc`, `120s`, `10mb`, `[]`).

FormSpec.description:
Input-dependent form of a polymorphic command.

A command with forms binds by the kind of its input: the form whose
`input` contains the input kind applies. The first form is the primary
form; the `position` and `required` attributes of the parameters describe
it.

output.description: Output kinds of the form; empty means the output of the command.

positional.description: Positional parameters of the form, in order.

required.description:
Required parameters of the form; a name of an exclusive group means
"exactly one parameter of the group".

params.description: Parameters accepted by the form; empty means every parameter.

expand.description:
Parameter of a source form that names the entries the command works
on. The binder expands the form to an `info` head whose `path` is the
value of this parameter, followed by the command bound in its form for
`entry` input.
